definition: Having two opposite feelings about something at the same time.
examples: I feel ambivalent about moving to Canada; I want the job but will miss home.
She was ambivalent about the new boss.

pattern.example: He is ambivalent about marriage.

cloze.sentence: Voters seem ___ about the new tax and cannot decide.

formDrill.sentence: His ___ about leaving his job showed in his silence.

fix.wrong: I am ambivalent with the offer.
fix.right: I am ambivalent about the offer.

distractors: Strongly in favor of a plan.
Not interested in any result.
Angry and unwilling to talk.
tip: Ambivalent is not the same as indifferent; ambivalent people feel both ways.

definition: To shock or excite people into taking action.
examples: The news of the fraud galvanized the staff into action.
The coach's speech galvanized the team before the final.

pattern.example: The crisis galvanized them into working together.

cloze.sentence: A powerful speech can ___ people into taking action.

formDrill.sentence: The ___ of support after the flood was impressive.

fix.wrong: The news galvanized the staff for action.
fix.right: The news galvanized the staff into action.

distractors: To cover metal with a layer of paint.
To make a group feel tired and discouraged.
To slow down a project on purpose.

definition: Peculiar to one person; unusual in a personal way.
examples: His idiosyncratic way of filing papers confuses everyone else.
She has an idiosyncratic style of dressing.

pattern.example: He has an idiosyncratic teaching method.

cloze.sentence: The chef's ___ recipes use ingredients nobody else combines.

formDrill.sentence: Everyone has a few ___, like eating cereal at night.

fix.wrong: He has an idiosyncratic habit of talk.
fix.right: He has an idiosyncratic way of talking.

distractors: Normal and the same as everyone's.
Related to the study of the mind.
Based on strict rules and routines.

definition: Interested in learning and asking many questions.
examples: My inquisitive daughter asks "why" about everything.
An inquisitive mind is useful in research.

pattern.example: She is inquisitive about other cultures.

cloze.sentence: Good reporters are ___ and always ask follow-up questions.

formDrill.sentence: The cat sniffed the box ___.

fix.wrong: He is inquisitive of new things.
fix.right: He is inquisitive about new things.

distractors: Unwilling to speak to strangers.
Rude and quick to blame others.
Bored by long explanations.
tip: Inquisitive can sound rude if it means asking about private matters.
